# The cultural heritage sector makes the case for Public AI – Open Future

Today, the common European data space for cultural heritage, stewarded by the Europeana Initiative, published its white paper “[The case for Public AI: making it happen with cultural heritage](https://www.dataspace-culturalheritage.eu/en/news/making-public-ai-reality-how-cultural-heritage-can-lead-the-way).” This is an important publication from a sector that will be a vital pillar of the emerging Public AI ecosystem, and anyone working on public-interest AI should take note.

At its core, the paper argues that Europe does not have to choose between regulation and innovation, or accept that the foundations of AI will be set by a handful of private actors. It makes the case for a distinctly European, public-interest path, and it asks the cultural heritage sector to play an active part in building it: as a steward of high-quality, multilingual, well-documented data; as a reliable intermediary that can govern access and reuse on fair and reciprocal terms; as a contributor to smaller, domain-relevant models; and as an engine for public AI literacy. These are concrete, operational roles, grounded in the sector’s public mission. Together, they show where public institutions can make a distinctive contribution and how that contribution can correct for the current market-centric push to build European AI at any cost.

[The Case for Public AI](https://pro.europeana.eu/files/data_space/publications/The_case_for_Public_AI_PDF.pdf) is an important step on the road to the AI Strategy for the Cultural and Creative Sectors, which the European Commission has signaled for 2027. It gives the cultural heritage sector a clear, shared basis from which to speak with one voice and to define its position within an information ecosystem that is increasingly shaped by generative AI and the new information loops it enables. AI is a socio-cultural technology that is rapidly becoming the main interface through which people access culture and information, and the cultural sector must therefore play a central role in shaping how it is embedded in society. This raises important questions about purpose and governance that the forthcoming strategy will need to address. **The new white paper makes clear that such a strategy must not focus on AI adoption by these sectors, but on how they can shape the technology for better societal outcomes.**

## **Public AI takes hold**

Open Future was commissioned to write an early concept note, [AI, cultural heritage, and the public interest](https://openfuture.eu/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/260130ai_cultural_heritage_public_interest.pdf), which fed into this work and drew [on our earlier thinking on Public AI](https://openfuture.eu/publication/white-paper-on-public-ai/). But the credit for the white paper belongs to the Europeana Initiative, the data space community, and the more than 400 professionals who shaped it through the [Alignment Assembly on Culture for AI](https://publications.beeldengeluid.nl/pub/2542).

That is what we find most encouraging. It is one thing to argue for Public AI in a policy paper; it is another to see the idea resonate so clearly and concretely among the institutions that steward Europe’s cultural memory. When these organizations make the case in their own name and commit to a shared program of action, Public AI stops being a proposal made on their behalf and becomes a direction the sector has chosen for itself. We look forward to supporting that work as it develops.

# 文化資產部門為公共 AI 提出主張 – Open Future

今天，由 Europeana Initiative 倡議組織所維護的歐洲文化資產共同數據空間（common European data space for cultural heritage）發表了白皮書：[《公共 AI 的主張：利用文化資產實現公共 AI》（The case for Public AI: making it happen with cultural heritage）](https://www.dataspace-culturalheritage.eu/en/news/making-public-ai-reality-how-cultural-heritage-can-lead-the-way)。對於這個即將成為新興公共 AI（Public AI）生態系統重要支柱的部門來說，這是一份非常關鍵的出版物，任何致力於公益人工智慧（public-interest AI）的人士都應密切關注。

該報告的核心觀點指出，歐洲不必在監管與創新之間做出抉擇，也無需默默接受人工智慧（AI）的基礎將由少數私人企業所奠定。它主張走一條具有鮮明歐洲特色、符合公共利益的道路，並呼籲文化資產部門在建構這條道路上扮演積極的角色：包括作為高品質、多語言、記錄完善的數據守護者；作為以公平和互惠條款管理存取與重複使用的可靠中介機構；作為小型且與特定領域相關的模型貢獻者；以及作為提升大眾 AI 素養的引擎。這些都是具體且具操作性的角色，並立足於該部門的公共使命。這些角色共同展現了公共機構可以做出哪些獨特貢獻，以及這些貢獻如何糾正當前不惜一切代價、以市場為中心來打造歐洲 AI 的做法。

[《公共 AI 的主張》（The Case for Public AI）](https://pro.europeana.eu/files/data_space/publications/The_case_for_Public_AI_PDF.pdf)是邁向文化與創意產業 AI 戰略的重要一步，歐洲執行委員會（European Commission）已表明將在 2027 年推出此戰略。它為文化資產部門提供了一個清晰且共享的基礎，使其能以同一個聲音說話，並在這個日益受到生成式 AI 及其推動的新資訊循環所塑造的資訊生態系統中，明確定位自己的角色。AI 是一種社會文化技術，正迅速成為人們獲取文化和資訊的主要媒介，因此文化部門必須在引導 AI 融入社會的過程中扮演核心角色。這帶來了關於宗旨與治理的重要問題，而即將出爐的戰略必須解決這些問題。**意即這份新發表的白皮書明確指出，此類戰略的重點不應放在這些部門如何採用 AI，而應著重於他們如何塑造這項技術，以帶來更好的社會效益。**

## **公共 AI 逐漸落實**

Open Future 受託撰寫了前期的概念說明書：[《AI、文化資產與公共利益》（AI, cultural heritage, and the public interest）](https://openfuture.eu/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/260130ai_cultural_heritage_public_interest.pdf)，該文為此項工作提供了養分，並借鑑了[我們早期對公共 AI（Public AI）的思考](https://openfuture.eu/publication/white-paper-on-public-ai/)。不過，這份白皮書的功勞應歸於 Europeana Initiative、數據空間社群，以及透過[「文化與 AI 協同大會」（Alignment Assembly on Culture for AI）](https://publications.beeldengeluid.nl/pub/2542)共同塑造此書的 400 多位專業人士。

這正是我們感到最受鼓舞的地方。在政策文件中論證公共 AI 是一回事；但看到這個理念在守護歐洲文化記憶的機構中引起如此清晰且具體的共鳴，又是另一回事。當這些組織以自己的名義提出主張，並承諾落實共同行動計劃時，公共 AI 就不再只是他人代為提出的倡議，而是該部門為自己選擇的未來方向。我們期待在這項工作推展的過程中持續給予支持。
